Śṛṅga in the Rigveda^1 and later^2 denotes the ‘horn’ of any
sort of animal. Hence the ‘barb’ of the arrow is called its
horn in the Atharvaveda.^3
1) i. 140, 6; 163, 11; ii. 39, 3; iii. 8.
10, etc.
2) Av. ii. 32, 6; viii. 6, 14; ix. 4, 17, etc.
3) iv. 6, 5. Cf. Whitney, Translation
of the Atharvaveda, 154.
